## Positive Self-Talk {#positive-self-talk}

Positive self-talk does not require forced optimism. Start by noticing the words, tone, emotion, and body response that show up. Ask what you would say to a close friend in the same circumstances and what relevant evidence the difficult thought leaves out. Aim for a response that is fair, specific, believable, and supportive of effective action.

[Open the Positive Self-Talk tool](/tool-finder/positive-self-talk/). The [CBT balanced-alternatives lesson](/learn/cbt-anxiety/thought-records-part-2.html#balanced-alternatives) remains useful when the thought needs a more structured evidence review.

## Self-Compassion and Loving Kindness

Loving kindness and self-compassion can be practised through intention, language, and small caring actions. They make room for difficulty while reducing avoidable self-attack.

## Source / Printable Copy

[Other mindfulness perspectives: spiritual Wise Mind, loving kindness, and being/doing mind](/resources/mindfulness/mindfulness-other-perspectives-source.pdf)

## Text Version / Adapted Text

The source presents several perspectives rather than one required belief system. Loving-kindness practice intentionally wishes safety, health, ease, and wellbeing for oneself and others. Being Mind emphasizes awareness and presence; Doing Mind emphasizes goal-directed action. Wise Mind can hold both.
